subject: Rollout plan + release flag coordination: Optimize config versioning / safe-apply + rollback
body:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Rollout plan + release flag coordination: Optimize config versioning / safe-apply + rollback

Hey Connor,

We’re ready to align on the release/flag strategy for the Safe apply + rollback mechanism (config version history + one-click rollback) before we merge the last couple pieces.

Can you confirm the preferred flag approach for the Jan/Feb train?

What we need:
- Stage rollout: internal -> hosted sandbox -> hosted prod -> dedicated -> private
- Ability to hard-disable *writes* (apply/rollback) while keeping read-only history view available
- Kill switch if we see propagation issues (avoid split brain / stuck rollouts)
- Make sure we don’t ship the DB migrations “dark” in a way that creates a wedge for Private upgrades

Current implementation assumptions (can adjust):
1) Server-side gates (control plane) for:
   - creating new config versions
   - applying a version (safe-apply)
   - rolling back to a prior version
2) Console UI gate (hide entry points unless server gate is on + RBAC permission)
3) Runtime lock/lease feature (apply/rollback atomicity) has its own gate, but defaults ON once code deployed

Proposed flags (names tentative):
- optimize.configVersionStore.enabled (migrations + read path)
- optimize.configHistory.readOnly (console + API list/get enabled)
- optimize.safeApply.enabled (create/apply)
- optimize.rollback.enabled (rollback endpoint + UI)
- optimize.applyLease.enabled (runtime-side lock/lease; can force-off if issues)

If you’re up for it, I can send a one-pager “flag matrix” by environment + exact train dates.

Thanks,
Dylan

—
Dylan Brooks
Eng Lead, Console & Tooling
Redwood Inference



From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 10:03 AM
Subject: Re: Rollout plan + release flag coordination: Optimize config versioning / safe-apply + rollback

Yep, makes sense. A few constraints from release train side:

- We can ship DB migrations in the train even if the feature is gated, but we need:
  (a) migrations are backward compatible with the previous app version
  (b) no startup hard dependency on new tables when flags are OFF
- For Private: we need the installer/upgrade step to be able to apply migrations deterministically, and we should avoid any “migrations included but unused” breaking backup/restore scripts.

Flag preference:
- Keep it simple at first: 1-2 server-side gates we can reason about.
- BUT agree we need separate read-only vs write paths.

How about we collapse:
- optimize.configVersionStore.enabled -> always ON once deployed (tables exist; read path is safe)
- optimize.configHistory.enabled -> enables list/get endpoints + Console history view
- optimize.configWrites.enabled -> enables create/apply/rollback endpoints (still enforced by RBAC)

Then optionally:
- optimize.applyLease.enabled -> keep as separate kill-switch if runtime leases are the risky part.

If you can send the matrix + which PRs land in which train, I’ll align with the train checklist.

Connor

—
Connor O'Brien
Release Train Lead
Redwood Inference



From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Leila Farouk <leila.farouk@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 4:38 PM
Subject: Re: Rollout plan + release flag coordination: Optimize config versioning / safe-apply + rollback

Got it. Collapsing is fine.

Updated proposal:

FLAGS
1) optimize.configHistory.enabled
- ON: list/get version history APIs, compare view, Console history timeline
- OFF: no surface area (except internal admin debugging endpoints)

2) optimize.configWrites.enabled
- ON: create/apply/rollback endpoints callable (still RBAC gated)
- OFF: read-only; any write attempts return 403 “writes disabled” and emit audit event apply_attempted/rollback_attempted with outcome=blocked

3) optimize.applyLease.enabled
- ON: runtime lock/lease required for apply/rollback (preferred default)
- OFF: runtime will accept applies without lease (we’ll keep this OFF option as emergency only; we will still do control plane optimistic concurrency)

ENV STAGING (initial)
- dev/staging: all ON
- internal prod: history ON, writes ON
- hosted sandbox: history ON, writes ON (limited to Redwood tenant)
- hosted prod: history ON first, writes ON after 1 week
- dedicated: history ON first, then writes ON behind allowlist of tenants
- private: history+write default OFF; enabled per-customer after installer upgrade

Release alignment (tentative):
- Train Jan 24: migrations + history read path + Console history UI (behind optimize.configHistory.enabled)
- Train Feb 7: write path (apply/rollback) + audit events + Console rollback flow (behind optimize.configWrites.enabled)
- Follow-on Feb: metric gates/canary apply (separate flag, see below)

Leila: any concerns with E2E coverage if writes are blocked in prod by flag? We can run full flow in staging, but I want a minimal prod smoke (history view + blocked write returns expected error).

Attaching the draft matrix.

Attachment: feature-flag-matrix_safe-apply-rollback.xlsx

Thanks,
Dylan



From: Leila Farouk <leila.farouk@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 5:11 PM
Subject: Re: Rollout plan + release flag coordination: Optimize config versioning / safe-apply + rollback

Works. For prod smoke we can do:
- list versions on a known route scope
- attempt rollback with writes disabled and assert:
  - 403
  - audit event emitted (rollback_attempted outcome=blocked)
  - no runtime propagation started

For staging E2E we’ll do full create -> safe-apply -> forced failure -> rollback.

Only request: please keep error payload stable for “writes disabled” so tests aren’t flaky.

-Leila

—
Leila Farouk
QA Automation
Redwood Inference



From: Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 9:26 AM
Subject: Re: Rollout plan + release flag coordination: Optimize config versioning / safe-apply + rollback

Adding a program mgmt note: Neha asked that we define the mitigation plan explicitly for on-call before hosted prod writes go live.

Can you include in the checklist:
- “turn off writes” steps + who has permission to toggle in prod
- what happens to in-flight rollouts (do they finish? cancel?)
- comms path (incident-bot message template + statuspage internal)

Neha/Sean want this as a gating item for GA in hosted.

-Talia

—
Talia Benson
Program Manager
Redwood Inference



From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 11:02 AM
Subject: Re: Rollout plan + release flag coordination: Optimize config versioning / safe-apply + rollback

Makes sense. Draft mitigation plan (will add to the release checklist + runbook):

Mitigation / kill switches
1) Toggle optimize.configWrites.enabled = OFF
- Effect: blocks new apply/rollback requests at control plane.
- In-flight rollouts: control plane will stop advancing stages; runtime agents should finish current “apply step” then report terminal state (stopped). We do NOT auto-cancel mid-step.
- Audit: emit apply_attempted/rollback_attempted outcome=blocked (with request_id if present).

2) Toggle optimize.applyLease.enabled = OFF (emergency)
- Effect: bypass runtime lease requirement; should only be used if lease path is wedged but we still need to rollback.
- Risk: allows concurrent writes if multiple operators attempt changes; we’ll pair this with a policy to have a single operator and a temporary “maintenance window” note.

3) DB-level mitigation (last resort)
- If we suspect the version store is causing load: we can leave history UI OFF (optimize.configHistory.enabled=OFF) and the control plane won’t hit the read path except internal debugging.

Permissions / access
- Only Release Eng + SRE on-call can toggle prod flags (we’ll confirm the group membership).

Comms
- incident-bot posts on:
  - write enabled
  - write disabled
  - apply/rollback failure rate > threshold

Connor: can you confirm which team owns the actual prod toggle rights today? I think it’s Release Eng + SRE but want it explicit.

Dylan



From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 17, 2025 at 2:40 PM
Subject: Re: Rollout plan + release flag coordination: Optimize config versioning / safe-apply + rollback

Prod flag rights:
- Release Eng on-call (rotating)
- SRE on-call (primary)

We can grant Console/Tooling one “break glass” role for Dylan/Chloe if needed, but default should be SRE/Release only.

One tweak: please make optimize.configWrites.enabled check *early* (before we allocate rollout jobs) so turning it OFF reduces blast radius quickly.

Also can you add a note about “rollback of the rollback feature” (i.e., if Console rollback UI is buggy, we can keep backend writes ON but hide UI entry points)?

Connor



From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 20, 2025 at 9:18 AM
Subject: Re: Rollout plan + release flag coordination: Optimize config versioning / safe-apply + rollback

Agree on early check — we’ll do the writes-enabled gate before:
- diff generation
- rollout plan creation
- runtime propagation enqueue

“Rollback of rollback feature” plan:
- Console has its own UI gate: console.optimizeConfigRollbackUI.enabled
  - OFF: hides rollback button/entry points
  - Backend can still accept rollback requests from internal tooling/API (subject to RBAC + configWrites flag)
- Similarly for safe-apply wizard entry: console.optimizeConfigSafeApplyUI.enabled

So in the worst case:
- Keep backend ON for SRE to rollback via API
- Hide UI if the UX is causing operator mistakes

Attaching the updated checklist with these items incorporated.

Attachment: safe-apply-rollout-checklist_v3.pdf

Dylan



From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 28, 2025 at 4:47 PM
Subject: Re: Rollout plan + release flag coordination: Optimize config versioning / safe-apply + rollback

Thanks. This is in good shape.

SRE asks before hosted prod writes go live:
- a single dashboard link in the checklist (config apply success/failure + stuck rollouts)
- confirm alert thresholds for elevated apply failures
- runbook includes exact flag names + where to toggle

Once those are in, I’m good to sign off for hosted prod staged enablement.

Neha

—
Neha Kapoor
Reliability Sponsor (SRE)
Redwood Inference
